extracted.intended_audience: 19th-century planters, overseers, and military administrators (Department of the Gulf) managing plantations and compensated plantation labor
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and regulatory guidance for managing plantation labor, stock, implements, provisions, and discipline under both private overseer practice and Union Army free-labor regulations (Department of the Gulf, 1864).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timely clothing
rubrics_metrics.description: Have their clothing ready in good season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure summer and winter clothing are provided; spin and weave winter clothing on the place when practicable; dedicate a room under an experienced woman to spin yarn using convalescent or light-duty women so that clothing needs for the plantation are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange indoor employment in wet weather
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange profitable in-door employment in wet weather.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide light, useful tasks (e.g., spinning, weaving) for those who may be complaining or convalescent; use indoor work to maintain productivity and reduce idleness during bad weather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply wholesome, well-cooked food at regular hours
rubrics_metrics.description: See that an abundant supply of wholesome, well-cooked food, including plenty of vegetables, be supplied to them at regular hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide generous, regular rations to reduce sickness and theft; keep store-houses locked; guard against waste of provision crops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Care for the sick and convalescent
rubrics_metrics.description: The sick be cheered and encouraged, and some extra comforts allowed them, and the convalescent not exposed to the chances of a relapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide additional comforts for the ill, avoid exposing convalescents; exercise judicious medical care rather than indiscriminate bleeding or dosing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for nursing women and infants
rubrics_metrics.description: Women, whilst nursing, be kept as near to the nursery as possible, but at no time allowed to suckle their children when overheated; that the infant be nursed three times during the day, in addition to the morning and evening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect nursing mothers from extremes of heat and ensure infants receive additional daytime feedings beyond morning and evening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit whisky and provide cool water
rubrics_metrics.description: That no whisky be allowed upon the place at any time or under any circumstances; but that they have, whilst heated and at work, plenty of pure, cool water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ban intoxicating drinks to maintain order and health; ensure abundant clean water for workers when heated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent harmful carrying practices
rubrics_metrics.description: That care be taken to prevent the hands from carrying their baskets full of cotton on their head--a most injurious practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage or forbid practices that cause physical harm through instruction and supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose competent stock-minder and enforce strict stock-care system
rubrics_metrics.description: Spare yourself trouble by your choice of a stock-minder, and by adopting and enforcing a strict system in the care of the stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign clear responsibility for animals and enforce rules; overseers often neglect stock-care so a reliable appointed stock-minder reduces problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stable and hostler responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Put your stable in good order; and, if possible, inclose it so that it can be kept under lock. Place a steady, careful old man there as hostler, making him responsible for every thing, and that directly to yourself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hostler should have direct accountability to the overseer; hostler duties include preparing feed, keeping stalls littered and cleaned, attending sick animals, and maintaining gears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Horse and mule feed economy and work limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep horses or mules fat at the least expense of corn and fodder by feeding green crops and give teams from eight to nine hours per day of actual work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use oats, millet, peas, broadcast corn, Bermuda/crab-grass hay fed green at proper growth stages with a noon feed of dry oats or corn-chop; work teams briskly in shorter periods for efficiency and allow leisure for tool upkeep.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit work oxen and provide economical winter feed
rubrics_metrics.description: No more work oxen should be retained than can be kept at all times in good order; in winter well-boiled cotton-seed with a couple of quarts of meal per head, turnips, soaked corn-cobs, shucks, pea-vines, etc., are cheaper and better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain only as many cattle as can be adequately fed; use alternative feeds and preparation methods (boiling, soaking, cutting) to sustain condition at lower cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect young stock growth and handle failing animals
rubrics_metrics.description: When young stock of any kind are stinted of their proper food, and their growth receives a check, they never can wholly recover it. Let the calves have a fair share of milk, and also as much of the cooked food prepared for the cows and oxen as they will eat... When cows or oxen show symptoms of failing, from age or otherwise, fatten them off at once; and if killed for the use of the place, save the hide carefully--rubbing at least two quarts of salt upon it; then roll up for a day or two, when it may be stretched and dried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize nourishment for young animals to ensure lifetime productivity; fatten and preserve useful byproducts like hides properly when culling older animals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hog management: stocking rate, grazing, dedicated caregiver, and swill preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: One good brood sow for every five hands on a place is amply sufficient. Provide at least two good grazing lots (Bermuda, crab-grass, or clover), give a steady, trusty hand no other work to do but to feed and care for them, and feed a full mess twice a day of swill thoroughly cooked and allowed to become sour before being fed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain appropriate stocking rates, dedicated labor, grazing improvements (plaster to fields), and strict swill recipe (cotton-seed, corn-meal, ashes, salt, turnips/greens) cooked thoroughly and soured for best results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheep stocking guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheep may be under the charge of the stock-minder; from ten to twenty to the hand may be generally kept with advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign sheep to stock-minder and maintain moderate stocking density per hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sick animals deserve judicious, studied treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Sick animals require close and judicious attention... Study the subject of the diseases of animals during your leisure evenings. Think before you act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid indiscriminate bleeding/purging/dosing; follow disease-appropriate measures such as avoiding stimulants for fever, using bleeding or purging only when reasoned, provide moist, light, easily-digested food, cool drinks, rest and quiet; do nothing without a reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tool and implement record-keeping and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: The implements and tools require a good deal of looking after. By keeping a memorandum of the distribution of any set of tools, they will be much more likely to be forthcoming at the end of the month. Axes, hoes, and other small tools... should have his number marked upon it with a steel punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a distribution memorandum, mark tools with owner's number, and enforce the single rule: 'Have a place for every thing, and see that every thing is in its place.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic production and employment of women in textile work
rubrics_metrics.description: Few instances of good management will better please an employer than that of having all of the winter clothing spun and woven on the place. By having a room devoted to that purpose... more than enough of both cotton and woolen yarn can be spun for the supply of the place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish an organized domestic textile production room to supply clothing needs and employ light-duty women productively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save and properly house provision crops; avoid waste
rubrics_metrics.description: Rarely is provision saved without great and inexcusable waste, and fed out without still greater. His conduct should be the very opposite of this--an honorable, right-thinking man will feel a particular degree of pride in leaving every thing in thorough order, and especially an abundant supply of all kinds of feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overseers should take pride in conserving provisions and leaving supplies well stored to establish a positive reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous improvements to the land and infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Few plantations are so rich in soil as not to be improved by manure. Inform yourself of the best means... Draining, ditching, circling, hedging, road-making, building, etc., may all be effected to a greater or less extent every season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement site-appropriate soil improvements and infrastructure projects when opportunities arise; employers commonly reward such efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-improvement through agricultural reading and study
rubrics_metrics.description: During the long evenings of winter improve your own mind and the knowledge of your profession by reading and study. The many excellent agricultural periodicals and books now published afford good and cheap opportunities for this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use leisure time to study agricultural literature to improve management skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm but gentle discipline with consistent, measured punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: It is indispensable that you exercise judgment and consideration in the management of the negroes under your charge. Be firm, and, at the same time, gentle in your control. Never display yourself before them in a passion; and even if inflicting the severest punishment, do so in a mild, cool manner... When you find it necessary to use the whip... apply it slowly and deliberately, and to the extent you had determined... The indiscriminate, constant, and excessive use of the whip is altogether unnecessary and inexcusable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid passion-driven punishments; determine penalty beforehand and execute calmly; prefer milder, controlled punishments; use punishment consistently and without favoritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer confinement (stocks) and measured deprivation to whipping
rubrics_metrics.description: When it can be done without a too great loss of time, the stocks offer a means of punishment greatly to be preferred. So secured, in a lonely, quiet place, where no communication can be held with any one, nothing but bread and water allowed, and the confinement extending from Saturday, when they drop work, until Sabbath evening, will prove much more effectual in preventing a repetition of the offense, than any amount of whipping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use confinement and deprivation of comforts as an effective punishment alternative to excessive whipping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never threaten unless ready to punish; keep your word
rubrics_metrics.description: Never threaten a negro, but if you have occasion to punish, do it at once, or say nothing until ready to do so... Always keep your word with them, in punishments as well as in rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain credibility by following through on stated penalties and rewards to build a perception of principled governance rather than impulse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat all alike and avoid favoritism; reward good conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Never forgive that in one that you would punish in another, but treat all alike, showing no favoritism. Whenever an opportunity is afforded you for rewarding continued good behavior, do not let it pass--occasional rewards have a much better effect than frequent punishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent application of rules and occasional positive reinforcement are recommended for effective management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain discipline through regular patrols and supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: By taking frequent strolls about the premises, including of course the quarter and stock yards, during the evening, and at least twice a week during the night, you will put a more effectual stop to any irregularities than by the most severe punishments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular visible supervision, including evening and night walks, deters irregularities more than harsher punishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral and religious instruction supports good behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: You will find that an hour devoted, every Sabbath morning, to their moral and religious instruction, would prove a great aid to you in bringing about a better state of things among the negroes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize weekly religious/moral instruction sessions; empirical experience cited as producing improved cleanliness and Sabbath conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'fine crop' (multi-part standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fine crop consists, first, in an increase in the number, and a marked improvement in the condition and value, of the negroes; second, an abundance of provision of all sorts for man and beast, carefully saved and properly housed; third, both summer and winter clothing made at home; also leather tanned, and shoes and harness made, when practicable; fourth, an improvement in the productive qualities of the land, and in the general condition of the plantation; fifth, the team and stock generally, with the farming implements and the buildings, in fine order at the close of the year; and young hogs more than enough for next year's killing; then, as heavy a crop of cotton, sugar, or rice as could possibly be made under these circumstances, sent to market in good season, and of prime quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this multi-factor checklist to evaluate overall plantation success rather than judging solely by raw commodity output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flogging and other cruel punishments interdicted (General Order VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flogging and other cruel or unusual punishments are interdicted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Department of the Gulf regulations, cruelty in punishment is expressly forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain rolls of employed persons and preserve family unity (General Order VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Planters will be required, as early as practicable after the publication of these regulations, to make a roll of persons employed upon their estates, and to transmit the same to the provost marshal of the parish. In the employment of hands, the unity of families will be secured as far as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep official employment records and, when hiring, prioritize keeping families together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution by provost-marshal until tribunals established (General Order VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: All questions between the employer and the employed, until other tribunals are established, will be decided by the provost-marshal of the parish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on the provost-marshal as the interim adjudicator of labor disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for sick and disabled (General Order IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sick and disabled persons will be provided for upon the plantations to which they belong, except such as may be received in establishments provided for them by the Government, of which one will be established at Algiers and one at Baton Rouge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must care for sick/disabled on-site unless government establishments take them in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit unauthorized purchase from laborers and sale of intoxicants (General Order X)
rubrics_metrics.description: The unauthorized purchase of clothing, or other property, from laborers, will be punished by fine and imprisonment. The sale of whisky or other intoxicating drinks to them... will be followed by the severest punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers and third parties must not exploit laborers by buying their property or selling intoxicants; severe penalties enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit possession of arms without authority (General Order XI/XL)
rubrics_metrics.description: The possession of arms, or concealed or dangerous weapons, without authority, will be punished by fine and imprisonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control arms possession among laborers to maintain public order; authority required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor hours, benefits, wage schedule, and payroll rules (General Order XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laborers shall render to their employer, between daylight and dark, ten hours in summer, and nine hours in winter, ... receive healthy rations, comfortable clothing, quarters, fuel, medical attendance, and instruction for children, wages per month as follows... payment of one-half of which, at least, shall be reserved until the end of the year: For first-class hands $8.00 per month; second-class $6.00; third-class $5.00; fourth-class $3.00. Engineers and foremen, when faithful... $2 per month extra. This schedule may be commuted by consent at the rate of one-fourteenth part of the net proceeds of the crop... Wages will be deducted in case of sickness, and rations, also, when sickness is feigned. Indolence, insolence, disobedience of orders, and crime will be suppressed by forfeiture of pay, and such punishments as are provided for similar offenses by Army Regulations. Sunday work will be avoided when practicable, but when necessary will be considered as extra labor, and paid at the rates specified herein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow detailed hours, provide specified in-kind benefits, use the stated wage classes and reserve at least half wages to year-end; allow commutation to crop-share by mutual consent; enforce discipline with deductions/forfeiture per regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laborer choice of employer and one-year engagement (General Order XIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laborers will be permitted to choose their employers, but when the agreement is made they will be held to their engagement for one year, under the protection of the Government. In cases of attempted imposition, by feigning sickness, or stubborn refusal of duty, they will be turned over to the provost-marshal of the parish, for labor upon the public works, without pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow freedom to select employer but bind to one-year contracts enforced by government protections and sanctions for abuse/dereliction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow private cultivation allotments to laborers (General Order XIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Laborers will be permitted to cultivate land on private account... First and second class hands, with families 1 acre each; without families 1/2 acre; Second and third class with families 1/2 acre; without families 1/4 acre. To be increased for good conduct at the discretion of the employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit small land allotments to laborers to encourage independent industry; employers may increase allotments for good conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict commutation of supplies; pledge crops for wages (General Order XV)
rubrics_metrics.description: No commutation of his supplies will be allowed, except in clothing, which may be commuted at the rate of $3 per month for first-class hands... The crops will stand pledged, wherever found, for the wages of labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent employers from substituting supplies for wages except clothing at fixed rate; use crop pledge as wage security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage perquisites or share-cultivation to satisfy laborers and reserve yearly wages (General Order XVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is advised... that employers provide for the current wants of their hands, by perquisites for extra labor, or by appropriation of land for share cultivation; to discourage monthly-payments so far as it can be done without discontent, and to reserve till the full harvest the yearly wages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor perquisites or land shares over monthly pay to promote savings and stability; reserve wages until harvest where feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish Free-Labor Bank for safe deposit of wages (General Order XVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: A FREE-LABOR BANK will be established for the safe deposit of all accumulations of wages and other savings; and in order to avoid a possible wrong to depositors, by official defalcation, authority will be asked to connect the bank with the Treasury of the United States in this department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create secure deposit mechanisms for laborers' savings and seek government oversight to prevent embezzlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit transportation of laborer families abroad (General Order XVIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: The transportation of negro families to other countries will not be approved. All propositions for this privilege have been declined...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refuse proposals to move laborer families out of the department; protect family residency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overseers must adapt to new free-labor conditions or face penalties (General Order XIX)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overseer... is a relic of the past, and adheres to its customs. His stubborn refusal to comprehend the condition of things, occasioned most of the embarrassments of the past year. Where such incomprehension is chronic, reduced wages, diminished rations, and the mild punishments imposed by the army and navy, will do good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overseers must learn and accept new labor relations; failure to adapt may result in sanctions affecting wages and rations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor is a public duty; enforcement by provost-marshals (General Order XX)
rubrics_metrics.description: These regulations are based upon the assumption that labor is a public duty, and idleness and vagrancy a crime... The several provost-marshals are hereby invested with plenary powers upon all matters connected with labor, subject to the approval of the Provost-Marshal-General and the commanding officer of the department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat labor enforcement as a public responsibility; provost-marshals have broad enforcement authority subject to higher approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect impartiality of marshals; undue employer influence forbidden (General Order XXI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers, and especially overseers, are notified, that undue influence used to move the marshal from his just balance between the parties representing labor and capital, will result in immediate change of officers...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must not attempt to bias marshals; attempts to do so will prompt personnel changes to preserve fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government expectation of industry and conditional favor toward planters (General Orders XXII-XXIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful industry is especially necessary... All officers, civil or military, and all classes of citizens who assist in extending the profits of labor, and increasing the product of the soil... will render to the Government a service as great as that derived from the terrible sacrifices of battle... The liberal and just conditions that attend it cannot be disregarded. It protects labor by enforcing the performance of its duty, and it will assist capital by compelling just contributions to the demands of the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planters who cooperatively promote productive labor and contribute to public obligations will receive governmental favor and protection; non-cooperation risks forfeiture or loss of privileges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amnesty conditioned on unreserved future loyalty (General Order XXIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amnesty offered for the past is conditioned upon an unreserved loyalty for the future, and this condition will be enforced with an iron hand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political loyalty is a condition for amnesty and continued privileges; noncompliance entails loss of rights and options.
